name: Example Template
author: yakuda
description: A working plugin that shows every part of the plugin API at once: all setting types, all hooks, placeholders, and a custom widget. Enable it, open its Settings, and every control below is live - the labels update, the buttons do something, the log in the panel says which hook fired when. Copy the folder, rename it, delete what you don't need.

text: A working plugin that shows **every part of the plugin API at once**:
all setting types, all hooks, placeholders, and a panel of its own.
1. Switch it on and open its Settings - every control below is live.
2. Copy the folder, rename it, delete what you do not need.
3. Read `main.py` top to bottom; it is ordered the way a plugin runs.
This is the `about` key: a list of lines, or a block with
`"format": "markdown"`. `description` stays a plain string so an
older app - which cannot read `about` - still shows something

short_description: Copy this folder to start a plugin. Every setting type and every hook, live.

placeholders.mood: whatever the Mood dropdown is set to
placeholders.ticking: only present while Count ticks is on

_read_this_first: Everything a plugin.json MAY contain, switched off.
JSON has no comment syntax, so the convention here is a leading
underscore: the app keeps keys it does not know in Plugin.extra and
never acts on them, which makes _anything a safe place to park a
setting you are not using yet. To switch one on, move it out of
this block into the top level and drop the underscore.
This whole _reference block can be deleted. Nothing reads it.

_manifest._summary: older spelling of short_description - use one, not both

_global_placeholders._note: placeholders WITHOUT the plugin id in front, for a plugin that owns a name globally. Collides loudly if two plugins claim the same one, so use sparingly.

_chatbox._note: enabled:false = this plugin never writes a chatbox line. get_text() and get_lines() are not called and the block disappears from the card. get_values() keeps running, so {example_template_mood} still works. user_editable:true gives the user a switch - which is what this template has turned on at the top level.

_layout._note: order of the card's blocks: chatbox, settings, widget. Names you leave out are appended, so ["widget"] means 'panel first, rest as before'. This template uses ["settings", "chatbox"] at the top level.

_about_as_a_list._note: about also takes a plain list of lines when you do not want markdown

_enabled._note: true = switched on the first time it is installed. Rude unless the plugin is harmless and obvious.

_api._note: the plugin API this plugin CANNOT run without. Raising it locks the plugin out of older apps, so leave it at the lowest version that really works and feature-test with api.supports() instead.

_min_app._note: shown to the user when api is too high. Text only, never parsed.

_is_linux._note: false marks the plugin as not installable here. Both default to true.

_settings_types._note: every row type this app knows. label and hint are optional on all of them; key must be unique across the whole schema, groups included.

_settings_types.label: Read-only
_settings_types.default: text the plugin can rewrite with api.set()

_settings_types.label: Button
_settings_types._note: calls on_action(key); the returned text is shown
not a setting: puts build_widget() at this exact spot. May sit inside a group. This template has one at the top level, so its panel is above the settings rather than under them.

_settings_types.label: Only when on
_settings_types._note: hidden while _a_bool is off. depends_value takes a list for choice rows.

_settings_types.label: A type this app does not know
_settings_types._note: There is no "hologram" type and there never will be - it is a made-up name. Paste this row back into settings to see what an app does with a type it does not recognise: the row is kept, its value stays readable through api.get(), and the UI says so instead of dropping it silently.

_files._note: Files a plugin folder may contain. Only 'main' from the top level is imported by the app; everything else is up to you, and anything not imported is simply dead weight the app never touches.
_files.main.py: the entry point named by "main" - hooks live here
_files.osc_advanced_example.py: INACTIVE reference. Nothing imports it. Read the header before you copy anything out of it: you do NOT need a socket of your own for chatbox text or for ordinary VRChat parameters - the app already does both. It is only for a plugin that something OUTSIDE VRChat has to reach on a dedicated port: a hardware bridge, a heart-rate app, an OSCLeash-style second tool. Delete the file if that is not you.
_files.README.md: not read by the app - for whoever opens the folder
_files.configs/: written BY the app. Never ship one in your zip: it would overwrite the user's settings on update.

settings.label: What this is
settings.default: Every row below is one setting type. Hover any of them for the hint text.
settings.hint: A 'label' row is read-only. Its text is an option value, so api.set() can rewrite it at runtime - see the Status row further down.

settings.label: The panel goes here
settings.hint: A {"type": "widget"} row places build_widget() at this exact spot instead of underneath everything. It may sit inside a group too - that is how a plugin gets its panel above its own Connection block. The row holds no value and never reaches config.json; the key only has to stay unique.

settings.label: Try the blocks
settings.default: Grab a grip and drag: this card is set to "user_reorderable": true, so Settings and Chatbox swap places and stay that way after a restart.
settings.hint: Stored per plugin in configs/config.json under "layout". Your "layout" in plugin.json is what a user who never dragged anything sees.

settings.label: A checkbox  (type: bool)
settings.hint: The plain on/off row. Other rows can hang off it with "depends".

settings.label: A text field  (type: text)
settings.hint: Free text. Add "secret": true to mask it - shoulder-surfing protection only, it is still plain text in config.json.

settings.label: A dropdown  (type: choice)
settings.hint: The stored value is always one of the "value" strings, never the label. A plain list of strings works too, then value == label.

settings.default: You picked sleepy. This row only exists to show depends_value.
settings.hint: Shown only while the dropdown above is on a specific value.

settings.label: A number  (type: int)
settings.hint: A spinbox. "suffix" is cosmetic, the stored value is the number.

settings.label: A slider  (type: slider)
settings.hint: Same value range as int, different feel. Use it when the exact number matters less than the direction.

settings.label: An icon  (type: emoji)
settings.hint: A text field with the app's own icon picker behind the button.

settings.label: A path  (type: path)
settings.hint: Set "mode" to "file" for a file picker, and "filters" for the file types. The dialog is the native one on Windows and the platform one on Linux.

settings.label: Status
settings.hint: This one is rewritten by the plugin with api.set() - press a button below and watch it change.

settings.label: A button  (type: action)
settings.hint: Pressing this calls on_action("ping"). Whatever the hook returns is shown next to the button.

settings.label: A collapsible group  (type: group)
settings.hint: Groups hold other settings, including one more level of groups. They start collapsed unless "expanded": true.

items.label: Count ticks
items.hint: Switches the {example_template_count} placeholder on. Also shows that a setting inside a group is addressed exactly like one outside - keys are unique across the whole schema.

items.default: on_tick() runs once per chatbox frame, before the values are collected.

items.label: Still just a setting
items.hint: A third level would be kept as a locked row rather than dropped, so nothing disappears silently.

items.label: Everything back to default
items.hint: "style" is normal | primary | danger. Use danger for anything that destroys something.
